The Experience

One pot. Your call.

Every seat gets its own pot of simmering broth, a tray of thin-sliced beef rolled and ready to swish, a plate of farm vegetables — cabbage, mushrooms, squash, leafy greens — plus rice and our house dipping sauce.

How It Works

Swish. Dip. Eat. Repeat.

Shabu shabu is named for the sound the meat makes as you swish it through the broth. It takes about ten seconds to learn — and about fifty minutes to enjoy.

1

Pick your heat

Your pot of broth arrives already simmering. Start the vegetables first — they flavor the broth while they soften.

2

Swish the beef

Hold a slice of beef in the simmering broth and swish it back and forth. It's paper-thin, so a few seconds is all it takes.

3

Dip and eat

Run it through the house dipping sauce, eat it over rice, and go again. Finish with the vegetables and the broth they've been sweetening all along.
